reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent source-semantic review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP and Radare2 6.2.0 on retail igi.exe; the candidate translation unit was read from the working tree at the recorded digest.
review_basis: The current engine/src/retail/core/app_context.cpp hashes to b6ba8b5b6d1e337910c59bc20ee7a50299013b9b50cbf14f7e0f235aa0037823. Binary Ninja recovered the retail entry live at 0x0048F1A0 (11 bytes, 1 basic block, 0 edges, bytes 0fbe442404a3f88b5c00c3) and Radare2 independently recovered the same entry, size, signature and empty edge set. The candidate body was then read against that reconstruction. This review supersedes the earlier artifact, which bound a different implementation digest (398a6c72...) and whose check rationales described IFF chunk-tree behaviour that does not exist in this entry; none of that stale text is relied on here.

retail_function.name: AppContext_SetDebugged
retail_function.summary: 0x0048F1A0: 11 bytes, one block, no calls. movsx eax, byte [esp+4]; mov dword [0x5C8BF8], eax; ret. The only argument is read as a signed byte, written as a 32-bit dword to the app-level debug flag, and left in EAX.

candidate_function.summary: App_ContextSetDebugged(std::int8_t state): sign-extends the byte into std::int32_t, stores it in the debugged field of the port AppContextState (the representation of retail 0x005C8BF8, read back by 0x0048F1B0), and returns the stored value.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja and Radare2 both recover a function entry at 0x0048F1A0 with 11 bytes, one basic block and zero edges, and the two retail-image graphs agree 1.000. The candidate defines App_ContextSetDebugged at that scope; no other body is claimed.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Retail is cdecl int32_t(char): the single argument is the byte at [esp+4], sign-extended by movsx. The candidate takes exactly one std::int8_t and sign-extends it to std::int32_t. Argument count, stack slot, width and cdecl order are preserved.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The only constant is the retail absolute global 0x005C8BF8, represented as the debugged member of AppContextState and read back by the sibling getter at 0x0048F1B0. The body performs no scaling, arithmetic or table indexing, so no numeric constant can be mismapped.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: Retail performs exactly one 32-bit store, to 0x005C8BF8; every neighbouring global is untouched. The candidate performs exactly one int32_t field store and does not modify any other member of the port state. Access width (32 bits) and ordering (sign-extend before store) match.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: The retail body contains no call and neither does the candidate. The complete side effect is the single 32-bit flag store; the return value is not an output parameter or callback result.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Retail leaves the sign-extended argument in EAX and executes the single retn; there are no branches, no error path and no early return. The candidate returns the same stored value on its single path. No fallback or synthetic error behaviour was added.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: The body contains no floating-point load, store, conversion or arithmetic instruction on either side.

signature_comparison.rationale: Retail is int32_t(char arg1) under cdecl; the candidate is std::int32_t App_ContextSetDebugged(std::int8_t). The single stack argument, its one-byte width, the sign extension and the 32-bit EAX return are preserved; only the source language type spelling differs.

behavioural.method: Retail instruction bytes executed under unicorn x86-32 with the true PE image; the compiled candidate executed natively with the same synthetic state; returned dwords and the stored flag compared case by case. This is emulator/host execution, not a live paired game process.

limitations: The candidate represents the retail absolute global 0x005C8BF8 as a member of the port AppContextState; raw absolute-address identity is not reproduced.
This review covers the 11-byte retail body and the single candidate body only. No natural game reachability, concurrency or whole-game parity is claimed.

The behavioural differential is emulator/host execution (Unicorn retail bytes plus the compiled candidate), not a live paired retail/candidate game process; RUNTIME_TESTED and VERIFIED are not claimed.
cfg_similarity 1.0 is the retail Binary Ninja-vs-Radare2 graph score for a one-block body; it is not a candidate-vs-retail CFG score.

The previous semantic-review artifact bound implementation digest 398a6c72... and described IFF chunk-tree behaviour; it was stale against the current source and factually unrelated to this entry, and is replaced by this review.
